# INNO-TREC

## Overview

INNO-TREC is a Horizon Europe project on renewable and citizen energy communities. This system covers its visual identity (from the INNO-TREC Brand Manual) and the interface of its web tools: monitoring of consumption, PV production and storage; PV yield and performance; maintenance of community assets; and the Energy Credit Management System (ECMS), where community members hold, send and use energy credits.

The look is plain, flat and square: white grounds, a pale grey app background, square corners, thin borders instead of shadows, and the brand's green, blue and orange used as large fills and accents, never as text on white.

There are two audiences, and screens are designed for one or the other:

- **Members** (residents, small businesses, public buildings) often have little experience with digital tools. Member screens use plain words, large text and controls, one task per screen, short steps, and icons always paired with words.
- **Managers and administrators** run the community and need detail: identifiers, codes, data quality and full ledger records. Their screens can be denser.

The interface only displays what the backend reports and collects input. Credit calculations, limits, balance rules, eligibility, signing and recording all happen in the backend.

Where the brand manual is silent, values were sampled from its page layout or proposed for the interface; these are marked in the source design system.

## Colors

Three brand colours, each tied to a project theme:

| Token | Brand name | Stands for |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `green` #78b948 (`secondary`) | Renewables | Renewables, sustainability, growth, innovation |
| `light-blue` #1978b8 (`primary`) | Digital platforms | Clean energy, trust, connection, data |
| `orange` #ef7d1c (`tertiary`) | Community | Warmth, energy flow, inclusion, activity |

- Lead with `green` and `light-blue`; they carry the logo. Use `orange` as an accent.
- `light-blue` is the primary action colour (primary buttons, links, focus ring) and the only brand colour that may be text on `surface` (4.75:1).
- Never set text in `green` or `orange` on light grounds (2.4:1 and 2.8:1). On their fills, use `on-green` (= `ink`, 4.6:1) and `on-orange` (black, 7.6:1). White on `light-blue` is fine (4.75:1).
- Text is `ink` (#3f3b3c) on `surface`, `surface-muted`, the tints and `stone`; secondary text is `ink-muted`.
- `surface` (white) for cards and content; `surface-muted` (#f0f2f4) for the app background, header bands and table headers.
- Tints (`green-tint`, `light-blue-tint`, `orange-tint`, `danger-tint`) are grounds for badges, alerts and selected rows, always with `ink` text (or `danger` on `danger-tint`).
- `line` for dividers and card borders; `line-strong` for input and secondary-button borders (3:1 or more).
- `danger` (#b42318) for errors and destructive actions only. A balance below zero is not an error: show it with a minus sign in `ink`.
- Status always has a word and an icon as well as a colour: success (`green-tint`), information (`light-blue-tint`), warning (`orange-tint`), danger (`danger-tint`).
- Charts use four fixed series colours: `series-consumption` (= `light-blue`), `series-pv` (#d26a12), `series-storage` (#2f6b1a) and `series-grid` (#6b3fa0). Each series keeps its colour in every chart. The set was validated together: every pair stays apart for protanopia and deuteranopia, and every colour reaches 3:1 on `surface` and `surface-muted`. They colour marks only; chart text stays `ink` and `ink-muted`.
- `black`, `stone`, `stone-light`, `logo-grey` and `logo-grey-light` describe logo backgrounds and the greyscale logo files; they are not interface colours.

## Typography

- **Figtree Bold** is the primary typeface: headings and titles (`display`, `title`, `heading`). Section titles may be set in capitals, as in the brand manual.
- **Open Sans** is the secondary typeface: body text, labels, tables (`body`, `body-light`, `label`, `caption`). The brand manual uses it in Light and Bold.
- `mono` (system monospace) only for identifiers and hashes on manager screens.
- Corpta is the logotype's font. Never set text in it and never retype the logo; use the logo files.
- Both Figtree and Open Sans are free Google Fonts.
- Member screens: text at least 16px; important numbers large (the balance is 48px Figtree Bold); form labels 17px; input text 18px.
- Write amounts with their unit and thousands separators ("1,284 credits"); use a real minus sign (−) and + / − in activity lists.

## Layout

- Spacing steps: `space-1` 4px (icon to label), `space-2` 8px (inside components), `space-4` 16px (card padding), `space-8` 32px (between sections, page margins).
- App frame: a 64px white top bar with the landscape logo and the tool's name, a 232px side navigation on `surface-muted`, and the main area on `surface-muted` holding white cards. Under 720px wide, the side navigation becomes a horizontal row and page padding drops to 16px.
- Mark a card or section title with a short `green` rule (32 × 4px) above it, as the brand manual does throughout.
- Member flows are a single column, at most 480px wide.
- Touch targets on member screens: buttons and inputs 52px tall, list rows at least 60px.

## Elevation & Depth

The system is flat. There are no shadows: surfaces are separated by a 1px `line` border and by the contrast between white cards and the `surface-muted` background. Selection is shown with a tinted background (`light-blue-tint`), not a raised surface. The focus ring is a 2px solid `light-blue` outline with a 2px offset on every interactive element.

## Shapes

- Corners are square (`rounded.none`) for cards, buttons, inputs, badges, alerts and blocks, following the brand manual.
- `rounded.full` only for avatars, status dots and discs, echoing the circles in the logo symbol.
- `rounded.sm` (4px) is available for small controls where a hard corner reads harsh; use it sparingly.
- Icons are simple 24px line glyphs with a 2px round-capped stroke, in the text colour.

## Components

React 18 components are published under the global `InnoTrec`; the values above describe how they look. Data names follow the ECMS Technical Specification v1.0.

**Shared:** Button (primary, secondary, ghost, danger; small, medium, large; optional icon before the label), TextField and Select (visible label, hint, error with icon; a large size for members), Card, Badge, InlineAlert (info, success, warning, error, each with an icon and border), Icon.

**Forms:** Textarea, DateField and DateRangeField (the browser's date picker), Checkbox (a choice confirmed with the form), RadioGroup (one of two to five options, with optional descriptions), Switch (on or off, with the state also in words), Dialog (a modal on the browser's dialog element for one short task or a confirmation; cancel first, main action last), and PasswordField (a password with a Show/Hide button instead of a second "repeat" field).

**Member screens:**
- WalletBalance: the credit balance in large type with the word "credits", when it was updated, and large "Send credits" and "Exchange" buttons.
- BalanceStatement: balance at the start, one line per kind of activity, balance at the end.
- EnergySummary: electricity used from the community versus the supplier (a two-part bar with labels), energy shared, and the credits involved. Amounts only, never formulas.
- TransactionList: one row per movement with an icon, one plain sentence ("Solar energy you shared"), the date and a signed amount; whole rows open the detail.
- TransactionDetail: amount and plain description first; the full ledger record sits in a closed "Technical details" section.
- RecipientPicker: a searchable list of people with initials and a short detail; never a typed address.
- TransferForm: three steps (choose a person, enter an amount, check and send), then a result screen.
- SettlementRequestForm: two steps to ask the community manager to exchange credits for money; confirms that the request was sent and that payment happens outside the app.

**Manager screens:** AccountCard and AccountList (wallets in EC with type, ID, balance and status: Active, Suspended, Closed), StatTile, DataTable, Identifier (shortened ID with Copy), ConfidenceBadge (Certified, Measured, Estimated, Manual), PurposeTag in technical mode (raw purpose codes).

**Shell:** TopBar, SideNav (icon plus label per item; four or five items for members), Footer (EU funding emblem, funding statement and legal links on `ink`), AppShell, and AuthLayout (screens without a session: TopBar, one centered panel of at most 440px on `surface`, the same Footer).

## Do's and Don'ts

- Do use one `primary` button per screen, labelled with a verb ("Send credits").
- Do split member tasks into short steps with "Step 1 of 3" and a Back button, show a check step before anything moves, and a clear result after.
- Do use plain words for members: "credits", "send", "exchange for money", "community manager".
- Don't show members "EC", wallet IDs, purpose codes, hashes, "issuance" or "CEMA" outside "Technical details".
- Do let members choose people from a list. Don't ask them to type an ID or address.
- Do pair every icon with words, and every colour with words and an icon.
- Do write errors as one sentence saying what happened and what to do next; after a failed send, say that no credits moved.
- Don't show formulas, conversion factors or rule names to members; display the amounts the backend computes.
- Don't show "pending" or "failed" transactions: ledger records are final. Show requests waiting for the community manager as requests.
- Don't use `green` or `orange` for text on light grounds, or white text on `green` or `orange` fills.
- Don't colour negative balances red; community and dependent wallets are normally below zero.
- Don't add shadows, gradients or rounded cards; keep surfaces flat and square.
- Do keep text contrast at 4.5:1 or more and borders, icons and focus rings at 3:1 or more.
- Do use the logo files as supplied: full colour on light grounds, greyscale on dark grounds, clear space of logo height ÷ 4 on every side. Don't recolour, redraw, stretch or invert the logo.
- Do give each energy series its own fixed colour (`series-consumption`, `series-pv`, `series-storage`, `series-grid`) in every chart, with a legend and the unit. Don't use the brand `green` or `orange` for chart marks.
- Don't put two y-axes on one chart; use two charts that share the time axis. Show estimated values dashed and missing data as a gap, never as zero.
- Do show times in the community's time zone, not the reader's, and name the time zone on the page.
- Do draw references (history, community value, target) as a dotted `ink-muted` line with its name and value. Do draw bars in the series colour of the measure, from zero, square, never coloured by status.
- Don't overlay several sources of the same quantity; plot each source's deviation (%) from the reference source, with the tolerance as a `surface-muted` band.
- Do write the project name as INNO-TREC in text; INNOTREC (no hyphen) appears only in the logo.
